svg.title: CausalLab: action marginals do not determine a cross-world joint
svg.desc: Both models have uniform observed X,Y and outcome probability one half under both actions. Stable Y=U has half always zero and half always one. Flip Y=X xor U has half helped and half harmed. Multiplying marginals incorrectly assigns one quarter to each response type. These are supplied synthetic mechanisms, not identified effects.

svg.text: CausalLab | action marginals miss cross-world dependence
Same observed joint: P(X=x,Y=y)=.25 for every pair. Same action marginals: P(Y=1 | do(X=x))=.5.
Independent U,V ~ Bernoulli(.5), X=V. Only the supplied Y mechanism differs. No data or model search.
Shared-noise joint over outcomes Y0 and Y1
Dashed .25: naive product of identical action marginals (wrong here).
Shared-noise joint over outcomes Y0 and Y1
Dashed .25: naive product of identical action marginals (wrong here).
Given factual X=0,Y=0, the same noise gives (Y0,Y1)=(0,0) for stable and (0,1) for flip.
Y0 means Y under do(X=0); Y1 means Y under do(X=1). Both are evaluated on each same noise world.
Cross-world dependence requires structural assumptions beyond single-world observations and experiments.
Synthetic binary responses only. No monotonicity, learned causes, empirical benefit or real-world harm claim.
